name: Isaac Newton
known_for: Laws of motion, universal gravitation, calculus
biography: Isaac Newton was an English mathematician and physicist. His Principia (1687) set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation, and he developed calculus independently of Leibniz. He also studied optics and showed that white light is made of a spectrum of colours.

name: Albert Einstein
known_for: Special and general relativity, photoelectric effect, mass-energy equivalence
biography: Albert Einstein was a theoretical physicist who developed the theories of special relativity (1905) and general relativity (1915). He received the Nobel Prize in Physics for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, which helped found quantum theory.

name: Marie Curie
known_for: Pioneering research on radioactivity, discovery of polonium and radium
biography: Marie Curie was a physicist and chemist who carried out pioneering research on radioactivity. With Pierre Curie she discovered polonium and radium. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.

name: Charles Darwin
known_for: Theory of evolution by natural selection
biography: Charles Darwin was a naturalist whose observations on the voyage of HMS Beagle led to the theory of evolution by natural selection, published in On the Origin of Species (1859).

name: Galileo Galilei
known_for: Telescopic astronomy, moons of Jupiter, support for heliocentrism
biography: Galileo Galilei was an astronomer and physicist who improved the telescope and observed the four largest moons of Jupiter, the phases of Venus and sunspots. His support for heliocentrism brought him into conflict with the Church.

name: Nikola Tesla
known_for: Alternating current induction motor, polyphase AC systems
biography: Nikola Tesla was an inventor and electrical engineer best known for the alternating current (AC) induction motor and polyphase AC power systems, which became the basis of modern electricity distribution.

name: Ada Lovelace
known_for: Notes on the Analytical Engine, often called the first computer program
biography: Ada Lovelace was a mathematician who wrote extensive notes on Charles Babbage's proposed Analytical Engine. Her notes include an algorithm for computing Bernoulli numbers, often described as the first published computer program.

name: Alan Turing
known_for: Turing machine, codebreaking at Bletchley Park, Turing test
awards: Officer of the Order of the British Empire
biography: Alan Turing was a mathematician and computer scientist who formalised computation with the Turing machine. During the Second World War he led work at Bletchley Park that broke the German Enigma cipher, and he later proposed the Turing test for machine intelligence.

name: Rosalind Franklin
known_for: X-ray diffraction images of DNA, including Photo 51
biography: Rosalind Franklin was a chemist and X-ray crystallographer. Her X-ray diffraction images of DNA, especially Photo 51, were critical to understanding the double helix structure.

name: Gregor Mendel
known_for: Laws of inheritance from pea plant experiments
biography: Gregor Mendel was a friar and scientist whose experiments with pea plants established the basic laws of inheritance. His work was largely ignored until it was rediscovered around 1900.

name: Louis Pasteur
known_for: Pasteurization, germ theory, rabies vaccine
biography: Louis Pasteur was a chemist and microbiologist who showed that microorganisms cause fermentation and disease. He developed pasteurization and vaccines for anthrax and rabies.

name: Dmitri Mendeleev
known_for: Periodic table of the elements
biography: Dmitri Mendeleev was a chemist who arranged the known elements into the periodic table in 1869 and predicted the properties of elements that had not yet been discovered, such as gallium and germanium.

name: Michael Faraday
known_for: Electromagnetic induction, electrolysis
biography: Michael Faraday was a scientist who discovered electromagnetic induction and established the laws of electrolysis. His work made electric motors and generators possible.

name: James Clerk Maxwell
known_for: Classical theory of electromagnetism, Maxwell's equations
biography: James Clerk Maxwell was a physicist who unified electricity, magnetism and light in a single theory described by Maxwell's equations. He also contributed to the kinetic theory of gases.

name: Niels Bohr
known_for: Bohr model of the atom, complementarity
biography: Niels Bohr was a physicist who proposed a model of the atom in which electrons occupy discrete energy levels. He was a central figure in the development of quantum mechanics.

name: Max Planck
known_for: Quantum theory, Planck constant
biography: Max Planck was a theoretical physicist whose work on black-body radiation introduced the idea that energy is emitted in discrete quanta, the starting point of quantum theory.

name: Richard Feynman
known_for: Quantum electrodynamics, Feynman diagrams
biography: Richard Feynman was a theoretical physicist known for his work on quantum electrodynamics and for inventing Feynman diagrams. He was also a celebrated teacher and writer.

name: Stephen Hawking
known_for: Hawking radiation, black hole thermodynamics, A Brief History of Time
biography: Stephen Hawking was a theoretical physicist and cosmologist who predicted that black holes emit radiation, now called Hawking radiation. His book A Brief History of Time became an international bestseller.

name: Katherine Johnson
known_for: Orbital mechanics calculations for NASA crewed spaceflights
biography: Katherine Johnson was a mathematician at NASA whose calculations of orbital mechanics were critical to the first American crewed spaceflights, including John Glenn's orbit of the Earth.

name: Barbara McClintock
known_for: Discovery of transposons, the so-called jumping genes
awards: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1983
biography: Barbara McClintock was a cytogeneticist who discovered genetic transposition in maize, showing that genes can move within a genome.

name: Johannes Kepler
known_for: Laws of planetary motion
biography: Johannes Kepler was an astronomer who formulated three laws of planetary motion, describing elliptical orbits around the Sun. His work provided a foundation for Newton's theory of gravitation.

name: Nicolaus Copernicus
known_for: Heliocentric model of the solar system
biography: Nicolaus Copernicus was an astronomer who proposed a model of the universe with the Sun, rather than the Earth, at its centre. His book De revolutionibus orbium coelestium was published in 1543.

name: Alexander Fleming
known_for: Discovery of penicillin
awards: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1945
biography: Alexander Fleming was a physician and microbiologist who discovered penicillin in 1928 after noticing that a mould had killed bacteria in a culture dish.

name: Dorothy Hodgkin
known_for: X-ray crystallography of penicillin, vitamin B12 and insulin
biography: Dorothy Hodgkin was a chemist who used X-ray crystallography to determine the structures of penicillin, vitamin B12 and insulin.

name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
known_for: Number theory, infinite series, continued fractions
biography: Srinivasa Ramanujan was a largely self-taught mathematician who made major contributions to number theory, infinite series and continued fractions, working with G. H. Hardy at Cambridge.

name: Chien-Shiung Wu
known_for: Wu experiment showing parity violation in weak interactions
biography: Chien-Shiung Wu was an experimental physicist whose 1956 experiment showed that parity is not conserved in weak interactions. She also worked on the Manhattan Project.

name: Tu Youyou
known_for: Discovery of artemisinin for treating malaria
awards: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2015
biography: Tu Youyou is a pharmaceutical chemist who discovered artemisinin, a drug that has saved millions of lives from malaria. She drew on traditional Chinese medicine texts in her search.

name: Jane Goodall
known_for: Long-term study of wild chimpanzees at Gombe
awards: Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire
biography: Jane Goodall was a primatologist known for her decades-long study of wild chimpanzees in Gombe Stream National Park, Tanzania, which showed that chimpanzees make and use tools.

name: Carl Sagan
known_for: Science communication, Cosmos, planetary science
biography: Carl Sagan was an astronomer and planetary scientist who became known for popular science writing and the television series Cosmos.

name: Rachel Carson
known_for: Silent Spring and the modern environmental movement
biography: Rachel Carson was a marine biologist and writer whose book Silent Spring (1962) documented the harm caused by pesticides and helped start the modern environmental movement.
